speaker: Doctor
text: I notice you have yellowish coloring of your skin and eyes, which is concerning. Can you tell me if you have experienced any abdominal pain or nausea recently?

speaker: Patient
text: 20-year-old male. The patient was previously healthy and has been brought to the emergency department due to agitation over the past 24 hours. Family members have noticed a yellowish coloring of his skin and eyes over the past week. The patient has a history of occasional cocaine and ecstasy use, and drinks alcohol socially on weekends. The patient also admits to high-risk sexual behaviors without using appropriate protection.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of high-risk sexual behavior and new onset jaundice, I need to rule out acute viral hepatitis. REQUEST TEST: Hepatitis Panel

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of cocaine use and acute agitation, I suspect a toxic or metabolic cause rather than viral hepatitis. REQUEST TEST: Urine Drug Screen

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Cocaine: Positive, Amphetamines: Negative, Opiates: Negative, Benzodiazepines: Negative, Barbiturates: Negative, Phencyclidine (PCP): Negative

speaker: Doctor
text: The negative hepatitis panel and positive cocaine screen suggest a non-hepatic cause for the jaundice, or perhaps a different underlying pathology. To investigate potential hemolysis or other metabolic causes, I need to see your complete blood count and metabolic profile. REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count, Comprehensive Metabolic Panel

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Hemoglobin: 16.3 g/dL, Hematocrit: 47%, Leukocyte Count: 9,750/mm3 (Neutrophils: 58%, Bands: 2%, Eosinophils: 1%, Basophils: 0%, Lymphocytes: 24%, Monocytes: 2%), Platelet Count: 365,000/mm3; Bilirubin: 25 mg/dL (elevated), AST: 600 IU/L (elevated), ALT: 650 IU/L (elevated), TP Activity: < 40% (reduced), INR: 1.5 (elevated)

speaker: Doctor
text: Despite the negative hepatitis panel, your significantly elevated liver enzymes and high bilirubin indicate severe liver injury, so I need to rule out autoimmune or drug-induced causes. REQUEST TEST: Autoimmune Hepatitis Panel, Acetaminophen Level

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the severe liver injury with normal autoimmune and acetaminophen levels, I need to investigate other causes of acute hepatitis. REQUEST TEST: Wilson's Disease Panel, Ceruloplasmin

speaker: Doctor
text: The low ceruloplasmin confirms Wilson's disease, which explains the acute liver failure and agitation. DIAGNOSIS READY: Wilson's disease
